qt: to the Commission Dominique Bilde (ID) Subject:

Bangladesh benefits from the ‘Everything But Arms’ arrangement, which grants duty-free and quotafree access for all exports, except arms and ammunition1. In 2023, an editorial in the Bangladeshi financial daily The Financial Express predicted that Bangladesh would graduate from the LDC (least developed country) category in 20262. However, according to that same editorial, Bangladesh could expect to enjoy the current zero-duty benefits until 20293. The article also states that, under the proposed new EU GSP scheme for 2024-2034, post-LDC Bangladesh might well be able to access GSP+ facilities4. 1.
How does the Commission justify maintaining the ‘Everything But Arms’ arrangement for Bangladesh, especially after the Rana Plaza tragedy5?
Decision COM(2021) 412 final of 15 July 20216suspended certain provisions of Regulation (EC) No 810/2009. What is the Commission’s view of Bangladesh’s cooperation on migration at present?

at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.6.2024) Since the Rana Plaza disaster of 2013, labour rights, including factory safety, have been a priority for the EU in the bilateral relations with Bangladesh. Bangladesh is one of the Everything but Arms1 beneficiaries under the enhanced engagement conducted by the Commission and the European External Action Service. This process is incentivising progress on areas including the labour rights’ international conventions listed in the Generalised Scheme of Preferences2. It has allowed for constructive bilateral exchanges on labour rights over the last few years, leading to progress especially concerning factory safety. The EU monitors Bangladesh’s commitments under its National Action Plan on the labour sector and through monitoring missions. The latest Report on EU Enhanced Engagement was published in November 20233. Concerning cooperation on migration, following the Commission proposal for temporary restrictive visa measures under Article 25a of the Visa Code4 adopted on 15 July 20215, there is an enhanced engagement with Bangladesh on readmission, resulting in a better implementation of the existing readmission arrangement. The Commission is continuously and closely monitoring the progress. The EU and Bangladesh hold regular high-level and expert meetings to discuss migration in a comprehensive manner and the Commissioner for Home Affairs proposed to launch a migration and mobility dialogue during her visit to Bangladesh on 10-11 November 2022. On 5 March 2024, the second meeting of the EU-Bangladesh Migration and Mobility Dialogue took place in Brussels, back-to-back with the eighth EU-Bangladesh Joint Working Group on the implementation of the (non-public) non-binding EU readmission arrangement for the identification and return of persons without an authorisation to stay (signed on 20 September 2017), and the second Talent Partnership Roundtable.
